questions.title: BFS Order Fill
questions.description:
The scaffold defines MAXV as 50 and builds an undirected adjacency matrix g (g[u][v] = g[v][u] = 1) from the input (line 1: V E; then E lines, each an edge "u v", 0-indexed nodes).

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void bfs_fill(int V, int g[][MAXV], int src, int out[], int *outn)

It must run a breadth-first search from src and fill out[] with the visit order, setting *outn to the count. Dequeue nodes FIFO; when processing a node, scan neighbors in ASCENDING node index and enqueue each unvisited one (mark visited at enqueue time).

Input Format:
Line 1: V E. Then E edge lines. Last line: src.

Output Format:
One line with the BFS visit order, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= V <= 50, 0 <= E <= V*(V-1)/2, 0 <= src < V

questions.title: Campus Broadcast Order
questions.description:

The scaffold defines MAXV as 50 and builds an undirected adjacency matrix g (g[u][v] = g[v][u] = 1) from the input (line 1: V E; then E lines, each an edge "u v", 0-indexed nodes).

    void bfs_fill(int V, int g[][MAXV], int src, int out[], int *outn)

The scaffold defines MAXV as 50 and builds an undirected adjacency matrix g (g[u][v] = g[v][u] = 1) from the input (line 1: V E; then E lines, each an edge "u v", 0-indexed nodes).

    void dfs_fill(int V, int g[][MAXV], int src, int out[], int *outn)

It must fill out[] with the recursive DFS visit order from src (record the node, then recurse into each unvisited neighbor in ascending index) and set *outn to the count.

Input Format:
Line 1: V E. Then E edge lines. Last line: the entry src.

Output Format:
